argument_summary: The supportable position is narrower than an unqualified compliance claim. The admissible record supports aggregate readiness and monitored deployment as a general governance pattern, but it also shows a current legal-intake subgroup regression and shows that prior approval plus informal monitoring are only contextual. On this record, the packet should be read as supporting certification only in a caveated form: the current release documentation must reflect the current evaluation results and expressly disclose the legal-intake weakness for the named launch use case. That narrows the claim to fit the policy instead of relying on stale approval or treating monitoring comments as a substitute for reviewed mitigation.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to resolve the audit issue on the admissible record.
claims_about_policy: The policy standard is explicit: current release documentation must reflect current evaluation results, and material segment weaknesses must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved mitigation. The admissible evidence supports three policy-relevant points: aggregate readiness passed and no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred; prior approval of the same model family is context only because the current retrieval configuration and eval batch changed; and the present record does not show approved mitigation or risk acceptance for the current legal-intake regression. The defensible reading is therefore caveated compliance conditioned on current-release disclosure, not clean present compliance on prior approval alone.
concessions: The present record does not show approved mitigation, reviewed risk acceptance, or attached disclosure language for the legal-intake regression.
Prior approval of the model family does not by itself satisfy the policy for this release after the configuration and evaluation changes.
Informal post-launch monitoring comments are not enough, by themselves, to satisfy the policy predicate.
